I am a young woman, with incurable cancer, diagnosed very young after being ignored for a very long time. Understandably i developed severe PTSD around medical based traumas and trust issues.

A few of my neighbours are signed up with them too. I explained my situation to a doctor there and established a ‘trusted’ doctor for all my medical issues- which as i have cancer, i do require help fairly often and side effects are so hard to manage.
Over 5 years i built this trust.
At the start of this week i was being referred to paliative care (already so so difficult to cope with at 30 years old) by a gp at this practise. The next day i was texted, out of the blue, telling me i was being removed from their practise and i had 7 days to find a new one.
No warning. No legitimate issue. And i was given 7 days to completely uproot everything in my life that was medically stable and move.
The panic that caused was immense. The thought of being unable to access medical care with a trusted physician sent me into one of the worst panic attacks ive experience in years. Including very physical symptoms that i wont go into.
My mum, who is my carer, was absolutely horrified and terrified for me and my mental health. She rang the gp practise begging them to not do this as the catchment issue was brought up before i even joined and had never been an issue before. She was put through to the practise manager- who has always been pretty rude from what i had heard over the years. But this time we got to experience that first hand. She proceeded to repeat to my mum, who was sobbing, that my PTSD and my trust in the gp there was ‘not her problem’ this was continually repeated to my mum, the manager did not once listen to my mum, or even attempt to behave with any compassion. Eventually my mum raised her voice through tears and said ‘listen to me please, you are our gp practise, her ptsd is very much your practises problem’. At that point the manager hung up on my mum. My mum crumbled. Terrified this would cause me to shut down and refuse medical help or any of my cancer treatment- which had happened before. So i tried to call, less than a minute after my mum got off the phone. I asked to speak to the manager, the receptionist told me yes, then went on hold, came back and asked my name, went on hold again, and then came and said the manager had ‘just left’. I tried to leave a message with the receptionist, i got no where.
Mentally broken, my mum drove me to a local gp practise and begged them for help, explained my ptsd. Also explained what had happened and that we had 7 days to find a new practise.
We were told by that practise that having 7 days to uproot and move medical care is highly inappropriate. It should be 30 days. Its very fair to say that the treatment we had received was unprofessional and cruel.
On further advice from multiple sources, i have contacted NHS england and the IBV to flag this behaviour.
There are a good few really great GPS that work here, and i had mostly received good care here for years. Its a shame that this catchment area issue was handled with no understanding, empathy, compassion or professionalism.
If you do need a practise with a gentle compassionate empathetic vibe, i recommend going elsewhere, as this experience has left me feeling utterly betrayed and like i have been kicked in the chest.
